title: Module <zynq_soc> not found
body:
Hello,

I'm working on axu3cg board. The Vivado project can be generated, but they failed when I either tried to simulate or synthesize. Here's the error message: 
`ERROR: [VRFC 10-2063] Module <zynq_soc> not found while processing module instance <zynq_soc_i> [Wenquxing22A/hw/fpga/board/axu3cg/rtl/system_top.v:33]`

Interestingly in arm.tcl under axu3cg/bd it says that it's generated based on zynq_soc. But I've checked all folders and even their history but I couldn't find that zynq_soc design. Is zynq_soc some kind of IP or should it be generated? How should I get this working?

Thank you in advance

title: CPU hangs up when accessing memory just below MMIO address space

comments.body:
Hi imhcyx,
this bug is probably because access request at 0x7fffffc0 in L2 CacheStage3 was blocked and accidently flushed by the prefetch request in Stage2. Now we have fixed this bug in prefetcher so L2 Cache will not be accessed if the prefetch request is mapped into MMIO space in branch "bug-prefetch-mmio". Please let us know if works in your FPGA board and thanks for pointing out the problem!
@imhcyx Would you please have a try with the prefetcher disabled?

> @imhcyx Would you please have a try with the prefetcher disabled?

I've tried disabling the prefetcher and L2 cache before applying the patch above and no problem has occured.
@imhcyx What about only disabling the prefetcher but keeping the L2 cache enabled?

title: Unable to synthesize the design in Vivado 2021.2
body:
Hi, I'm compling the design into Verilog with command `make PRJ=myproject BOARD=pynq STANDALONE=true` and with default settings. However, the compiled code contains some depth-1 array in the `EmbeddedTLBMD` module, and when I synthesize the code with Vivado 2021.2, it says `[Synth 8-2913] Unsupported Dual Port Block-RAM template for tlbmd_3_reg` and reasons to cause this error contains `Write port has constant address.` and `Only 1 word in RAM `. These are both true. Array `tlbmd_0` to `tlbmd_3` does have only one element and address input is constant (beacuse the entry count of the ITLB declared in [NutCore.scala](https://github.com/OSCPU/NutShell/blob/cf7963435b824106690152507bb9312c159b8d5e/src/main/scala/nutcore/NutCore.scala#L116) is only 4, so `depth of the array` = [TotalEntry / Ways](https://github.com/OSCPU/NutShell/blob/cf7963435b824106690152507bb9312c159b8d5e/src/main/scala/nutcore/mem/TLB.scala#L161) = 1).

A simple way to fix this problem is by manually adding a platform-specific attribute `ram_style` to these signals repectively, and set the values to `registers`, as follows, so the arrays can be implemented with registers. (I don't know if the line contains the attribute can be added without users' intervention (by Chisel comilers))
``` Verilog
  (* ram_style = "registers" *) 
  reg [120:0] tlbmd_0 [0:0];
```
The `ram_style` attribute is also abled to be set using elaberation-time constrains, however an additional XDC file is required in this situation. I'm not sure which is the most appropiate approach to solve the problem.


The following is `EmbeddedTLBMD` module in the generated code, and only the array `tlbmd_0` to `tlbmd_3` are related to the issue.
``` Verilog
module EmbeddedTLBMD(
  input          clock,
  input          reset,
  output [120:0] io_tlbmd_0,
  output [120:0] io_tlbmd_1,

  output [120:0] io_tlbmd_3,
  input          io_write_wen,
  input  [3:0]   io_write_waymask,
  input  [120:0] io_write_wdata,
  output         io_ready
);
`ifdef RANDOMIZE_MEM_INIT
  // ......
`endif // RANDOMIZE_REG_INIT
  reg [120:0] tlbmd_0 [0:0]; // @[EmbeddedTLB.scala 51:18]
  wire  tlbmd_0_MPORT_en; // @[EmbeddedTLB.scala 51:18]

title: Bootgen error for pynq board
body:
I  follow the step in `/fpga/boot/standalone.md` and want to get BOOT.BIN for pynq-z2 .
Generate verilog for pynq first and create a project in Vivado
```
make verilog BOARD=pynq
cd $(NUTSHELL_HOME)/fpga
make PRJ=myprj BOARD=pynq STANDALONE=true vivado
```
Bitstream and hdf file has been generated successfully.
But after linking ps.hdf and fpga.bit, there is something wrong when `make bootgen PRJ=myprj BOARD=pynq STANDALONE=true`

```
hezf@thuos:~/Documents/chisel_test/NutShell/fpga$ make bootgen PRJ=m3 BOARD=pynq STANDALONE=true
cd boot && hsi -nolog -nojournal -notrace -source mk.tcl -tclargs m3-pynq true

The project's board_part property was not set, but the project's part property was set to xc7z020clg400-1. Valid board_part values can be retrieved with the 'get_board_parts' Tcl command. Where is the ‘device-tree-xlnx’ for pynq? 

Thanks a lot and happy new year!

comments.body:
We mistakenly introduced an absolute path that shouldn't appear in NutShell/fpga/boot/mk.tcl. You can try to clone the https://github.com/xilinx/device-tree-xlnx project, checkout to hash 73e546e, and then modify the setting of "device_tree_repo_path" in mk.tcl:24
https://github.com/OSCPU/NutShell/blob/4b656f32aea0687fe8c823b99a54dc76517c3a41/fpga/boot/mk.tcl#L24
Thanks a lot. I clone the project 'device-tree-xlnx', but can't find the hash 73e546e. After change the `device_tree_repo_path`, the problem is the same, `generate device_tree` failed.

Done! It is really a version error.  The default `device-tree-xlnx` is 2020.2. I down the [19.1 version](https://github.com/Xilinx/device-tree-xlnx/releases/tag/xilinx-v2019.1), and change line 24 in mk.tcl. 
It seems a new year gift!
